subject.title: [Bug]: cron agentTurn returns before foreground Bash subprocess completes — long-running executors are killed mid-stream, leaving partial state and a placeholder digest

question: Should this cron foreground-Bash variant be fixed as its own cron pending-tool success blocker, or folded completely into the broader Claude CLI long-work lifecycle contract?
rationale: The source supports the lifecycle gap, but the durable fix changes stable cron success semantics, message delivery truth, and Claude CLI process cleanup ownership.

options.title: Add a cron-specific blocker
options.body: Require isolated cron to treat pending foreground native tool work as not finished, so it cannot record `ok` or announce placeholder output before the work completes or explicitly fails.

options.title: Consolidate under long-work lifecycle
options.body: Route this through #102172 or #97919 only if that canonical work explicitly covers the cron green-status and announce-placeholder invariant, not just process survival.

options.title: Document unsupported foreground longwork
options.body: Declare long foreground native Bash inside Claude CLI cron unsupported and route users to command, on-exit, or exec/process flows with explicit failure diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Add a cron-specific blocker
recommendation.body: Require isolated cron to treat pending foreground native tool work as not finished, so it cannot record `ok` or announce placeholder output before the work completes or explicitly fails.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus has the strongest Claude CLI live-session history and has merged adjacent native-tool lifecycle mitigation, making them the best available decision owner.
